## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button-group ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge @base-ui/react class-variance-authority ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/separator](https://cadence.dev/r/separator.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | separator | `@components/cadence/separator/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/separator.json) | | button-group | `@components/cadence/button-group/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/button-group.json) | [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: separator](https://cadence.dev/r/separator.json) [Source files: button-group](https://cadence.dev/r/button-group.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. Keep `button-group/index.tsx`, `separator/index.tsx` and `lib/cn.ts` at the listed relative paths. Button Group imports Separator even when you do not render `ButtonGroupSeparator`; both components share the `cn` helper. Button Group and Separator are static T0 components in full, reduced and none modes; no motion runtime, provider or additional item-specific CSS is required beyond the base theme and Tailwind utilities. Keep their source files' `"use client"` directives. In Next.js App Router, a Server Component can render these client parts with serializable props. Calling the exported `buttonGroupVariants` function belongs in a `"use client"` module. Usage, Vertical, “Static text inside the group”, “A rule between two controls”, and the top preview also use [Button](/components/button). Install it when keeping those compositions: ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button ``` For manual installation, follow Button's Manual tab and copy every listed file, including its motion and provider helpers, into the same relative tree. Button adds `motion` to the package list above; its provider files are required imports, while wrapping the application is optional. Button's press scale plays only in full mode and is dropped in reduced and none. The group adds no animation. Usage, Vertical and the top preview also use `lucide-react` for their plus/minus icons. Install it when keeping those icons; Button Group and Button themselves do not require an icon package: ```package-manager npm install lucide-react ``` Keep Usage, Vertical and the top preview's existing `"use client"` boundaries for their state and event handlers. Put “Static text inside the group” and “A rule between two controls” in a `"use client"` module too: they call `buttonVariants()` from Button's client module, even though their links retain native navigation. The caller owns the zoom value, limits and actions; Button Group supplies grouping and layout, without a toolbar arrow-key model. ## Usage ```tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { MinusIcon, PlusIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { ButtonGroup, ButtonGroupText } from "@/components/cadence/button-group"; export function ZoomControls() { const [zoom, setZoom] = useState(100); return ( }>{zoom}% ); } ``` ## Vertical The vertical group stacks controls and keeps only the outer corners rounded. It does not create a toolbar keyboard model: Tab still follows DOM order. This zoom value is owned by this instance. ```tsx "use client"; import { useState } from "react"; import { MinusIcon, PlusIcon } from "lucide-react"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { ButtonGroup, ButtonGroupText } from "@/components/cadence/button-group"; export function VerticalControls() { const [zoom, setZoom] = useState(100); return ( }>{zoom}% ); } ``` ## Static text inside the group ButtonGroupText joins a non-interactive label or readout to controls. `render` changes its element without extra wrappers. This label is a span, and the adjacent link opens the actual registry guide. ```tsx import { buttonVariants } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { ButtonGroup, ButtonGroupText } from "@/components/cadence/button-group"; export function GroupWithText() { return ( }>Guide Registry ); } ``` ## A rule between two controls Specify the separator orientation separately from the group: a horizontal group needs a vertical rule; a vertical group needs a horizontal rule. ); } ``` ## When to use - Two to five controls that act on the same object: bold/italic/underline, cut/copy, approve/reject, a zoom stepper. - A segmented control where the current option is a button state (`variant="default"` vs `"ghost"`), not a radio group. - A label plus an action, where the label should read as part of the control — use `ButtonGroupText` for the static half. ## When not to use - More than about five options. Beyond that the shape stops helping and a `select` or a menu is faster. - Mutually exclusive choices that need arrow-key navigation and a form value. That is `toggle-group`, or a `radio-group` inside a `field`. - A single button. The group adds nothing; use `button`. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | ----------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | `ButtonGroup` | `orientation`, native div | `horizontal \| vertical`; `role="group"`, `data-orientation`. | | `ButtonGroupText` | `render`, native div | Static label; swapped element via Base UI `render`. | | `ButtonGroupSeparator` | `Separator` props | Vertical by default; `self-stretch`, `bg-input`. | | `buttonGroupVariants` | `orientation` | Exported for composing a custom group root. | The joining rules are `[&>*]` selectors, so any child that renders a `data-slot` — a button, an input, a select trigger — participates without a prop. `ButtonGroupSeparator` accepts Base state callbacks for `className` and `style`, merged after defaults. `ButtonGroupText` uses native string classes and style objects. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). The group does not animate. Adjacent buttons share a border, and the only depth cue is `focus-visible:relative` plus `z-10`, which lifts the focused control above its neighbours so its ring is not clipped. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | The buttons inside keep their own press feedback; the group never adds a second animation on top of it. ## Accessibility - `role="group"` needs a name: pass `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) when there is no visible heading. Without one, a screen reader says "group" and nothing else. - Tab order follows DOM order, not visual order. In `vertical`, keep the DOM order the same as the visual stack. - Icon-only buttons inside a group must each carry an `aria-label`; the group label does not name them. - Do not mark the active segment with colour alone — use `aria-pressed` on a toggle button, or a `data-state` attribute your CSS keys off. ## Responsiveness and performance Groups use intrinsic width and a caller-selected orientation; no breakpoint switches it automatically. Stack or constrain long groups at the application level rather than hiding focused controls. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. Base UI behavior requires hydration; native HTML behavior remains browser-owned. Composed controls retain their own dependencies and motion contracts. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Use `ButtonGroup` for actions on one object, `toggle-group` for a value the form reads. They look alike and behave differently. - Do not add gaps between children: the rounded/border collapse is what makes the group read as one control. - `ButtonGroupSeparator` is already `self-stretch`; do not set a height.
